title: Survey other AMD BIOS scrapers and compare access strategies
description:
Survey of prior-art AMD BIOS scrapers and access strategies.

## Comparison table

| Project | License | Vendors covered | Access strategy | Adaptable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [Rexzarrax/Biosup](https://github.com/Rexzarrax/Biosup) | **OSL-3.0** (copyleft) | ASUS, ASRock, Gigabyte, MSI (consumer desktop UEFI) | Selenium + chromedriver | Reference only — copyleft license forbids code copy |
| [wxlg1117/smc_updater](https://github.com/wxlg1117/smc_updater) | unspecified (= all rights reserved) | Supermicro (BIOS + IPMI) | Selenium + Firefox geckodriver, scrapes vendor support pages | Reference only — no license = no copy |
| [erik-smit/BooterMicro](https://github.com/zylon-internet/BooterMicro) | **MIT** | Supermicro (all boards) | Perl, parses `supermicro.nl/support/bios` index | Yes — parsing approach reusable |
| [ycomiti/Lenovo-Bios-Scraper](https://github.com/ycomiti/Lenovo-Bios-Scraper) | (unverified, repo 404'd at survey time) | Lenovo (consumer ThinkPad/ThinkCentre) | Bash; mirrors via Wayback Machine; falls back to archive when official link dies | Reference — Wayback fallback pattern is good |
| [mellowCS/FirmwareScraper](https://github.com/mellowCS/FirmwareScraper) | **MIT** | embedded routers (AVM/Fritz, etc.) | Scrapy spider per vendor | Yes — spider-per-vendor architecture matches our `VendorScraper` ABC |
| [firmadyne/scraper](https://github.com/firmadyne/scraper) | **MIT** | embedded devices (D-Link etc.) | Scrapy | Off-topic for AMD mainboards |
| [fkie-cad/linux-firmware-corpus](https://github.com/fkie-cad/linux-firmware-corpus) | **GPL-3.0** | embedded Linux firmware (10k images, 10 mfrs) | Has a `scrapers/` dir, but README states most are broken | Reference only — GPL-3.0 viral with our codebase |
| [LVFS / fwupd](https://fwupd.org/) | LGPL-2.1+ | Hardware vendors that publish to LVFS | `.cab` capsules over a public API | Almost no AMD desktop/server BIOS published here. Some Lenovo, some Dell. Not a viable primary source for AMD boards |

## Techniques worth adopting from the survey

- **Wayback CDX as a discovery channel** — Lenovo-Bios-Scraper does this as fallback; we already do it as primary for ASRock and MSI. Confirmed best-in-class for Akamai/Incapsula-protected vendor sites.
- **Wayback as archive sink** — ycomiti/Lenovo-Bios-Scraper auto-submits `archive.org/wayback/available` lookups; consider mirroring our scraped URLs back into Wayback for posterity.
- **Spider-per-vendor architecture** — FirmwareScraper validates our `VendorScraper` ABC pattern.
- **Range-request board ID** — our MSI scraper uses HTTP Range to read 8 KB ZIP headers without downloading 20 MB; nothing in the survey does this. Worth keeping/documenting as a contribution back.

## Techniques explicitly NOT copied

- **Selenium / chromedriver** (Biosup, smc_updater) — heavyweight, brittle, datacenter-IP detection still trips the WAF. Our existing Akamai bypass (browser-like User-Agent + Sec-Fetch headers from a residential IP) works for Gigabyte. CDX is preferred over both.

## Coverage gap relative to scope

None of the surveyed projects cover the *complete* AM4 + AM5 + EPYC + Threadripper + ThreadripperPro + Embedded matrix. Our existing four scrapers (ASRock, ASUS, Gigabyte, MSI consumer) already exceed Biosup's coverage.

## Outcome

Filed individual scraper issues per (vendor x board_class) — see related issues. Outstanding gaps (in priority order): EPYC server vendors (Supermicro, Gigabyte server, ASRock Rack, ASUS server, Tyan), Threadripper / TR-Pro extensions to existing scrapers, Lenovo / Dell / HPE server lines, Embedded.
